question:
RECOMMEND: APPROVE — advance to build.

Why: every ruling you gave is folded in, the riskiest mechanisms were exercised rather than assumed, and the two criteria that could never have passed honestly are replaced. Nothing in this spec now rests on an unread fact. Build has real work it can start.

DECISION EFFECT: approve advances 061 to build in a dedicated worktree and dispatches a build agent, which writes the extractor, the importer and their tests. Nothing is written to your live data by this approval — the import cannot run until you approve the normalization sheet (AC-14), and the staging rehearsal comes before any production write. Reject holds 061 at spec with your feedback.

ONE THING I NEED YOU TO CONFIRM, because I did not simply do what you said:

You said "use prod categories, make sure the sage tis the same." The first half is done: for a production run the mapping resolves against production's own Categories tab, and the run aborts before writing if any name fails to resolve. The second half — making staging match production — the design makes UNNECESSARY rather than doing it. Because the importer resolves category names at run time against whichever target it is pointed at, the two tabs are free to differ without any risk of mis-filing. Aligning them would be tidiness, not correctness, and doing it would delete what look like somebody's test fixtures (Test Cat, Antkee, ScrollTest from cat_023 on).

So: is run-time resolution enough for you, or do you still want staging brought into line as hygiene? Approving without answering means we leave staging alone, which is my recommendation.

ONE THING YOU SHOULD KNOW BEFORE APPROVING, which is not a decision but a loss:

2024-12-17 through 2024-12-31 have no columns in your workbook at all. The last fifteen days of December 2024 were never entered. No import can recover them, so 2024's imported annual total will be short by whatever you actually spent that fortnight, and the app will show nothing for those dates. The same applies far more narrowly to 2024-06-16, and to 2023-06-16, 2023-07-01 and 2023-07-03. If you expected the imported 2024 total to match your own records, this is why it will not.

artifacts.summary:
CHOSEN APPROACH: two scripts, not one. An extractor reads the archive workbook and writes a normalization sheet you review; an importer reads only the approved sheet and writes to the app. They are separate deliberately, so your approval sits structurally between them and AC-14 cannot be bypassed with a flag.

YOUR THREE RULINGS, FOLDED:
- 2022 OUT OF SCOPE. Enforced by AC-4, and the guard was exercised rather than proposed: columns A-C are byte-identical across all three year bands, so taxonomy cannot tell them apart. The extractor discovers bands from header rows instead of using hard-coded row numbers, and asserts no row dated outside 2023-2024 reaches the app. Reversing this later is a --years flag.
- STAGING GOES FIRST. Specced with its cost stated, not assumed away: load-local-env.js cannot aim any admin script at staging today, so that plumbing is required work in this feature. The staging rehearsal — snapshot, apply, verify, hand-add a row, undo, diff — is a precondition of any production write. The credential wrinkle is handled: only the staging service account can read your archive workbook, production gets 403.
- D4 = A. Recorded as your decision. See below: it costs you nothing.

D4 — YOUR QUESTION, ANSWERED BY PROBE. You asked "is there any expense records?" rather than deciding blind. It had never been asked of the data. It has now been, per column:
- Day columns holding data but carrying no parseable date: 0, in both years.
- The 15 duplicated December 2024 dates occupy 30 columns. ALL 30 ARE EMPTY — both members of every pair, zero populated cells.
- The 16 missing 2024 days and 3 missing 2023 days have no column at all, so can hold no cell by construction.
- Rows with an untrustworthy date: 0 of 774 for 2024, 0 of 893 for 2023. The share of either year sitting behind a date we would have to invent is 0.00%.
So D4 dissolves. Option A at zero cost — every one of the 1,667 imported rows carries a real, unique date from its own column header, and there is no manual pass to do. Option B, assigning a date a cell did not carry, is not implemented at all, so that failure cannot occur by drift or by a later flag.

THE RECUT CRITERIA. All three now rest on references we control, so your workbook's own ~12% internal disagreement can no longer fail a check meant to catch OUR bugs:
- AC-2 joins the app to the approved normalization sheet on a key and compares per-year sums EXACTLY in integer minor units, not within 1%. Both sides are artefacts we control, so a tolerance could only hide our own arithmetic error.
- AC-3 asserts no month-total column contributed a row, discriminated on the column-label cell.
- AC-4 asserts no row dated outside 2023-2024 reached the app, and that the extractor discovers bands rather than taking row numbers.
- The old AC-2's subject is not deleted: it becomes AC-15, which requires the variance report to exist and cover all 24 in-scope year-months while requiring the exit code to be INDEPENDENT of its contents. Its falsifier is making the run fail on a variance threshold — that is, reintroducing the old AC-2.

THE SECOND RISKIEST MECHANISM, AND THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED SILENTLY: category ids are not portable between environments. Read live rather than taken from source constants, staging and production Categories tabs both use cat_NNN and disagree from cat_023 onward. A mapping built and rehearsed on staging would have filed production rows under wrong categories while every id-exists check still passed. AC-9 now resolves each name against the target's own tab at run time and aborts before writing if any name fails to resolve; D3 gains a production pre-flight no staging rehearsal can substitute for.

THE NORMALIZATION SHEET, AND WHETHER YOUR EDITS SURVIVE: yes, and the mechanism is never-overwrite rather than merge-in-place. Generate aborts on an existing tab; re-generation writes a new version and carries your corrections forward by source coordinate rather than row position; an irreconcilable conflict exits non-zero listing the keys; a source cell that vanished becomes orphaned rather than disappearing. If the carry-forward is itself buggy, the previous version still exists untouched, so recovery is re-running the carry, not re-doing your work. AC-16 covers it.

EXPECTED SURFACE AND TOLERANCE: +1,050 net LOC across 6 files, tolerance +/-30%. Up from +700 across 4, deliberately — the extract/import split is what makes your approval structural rather than procedural.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: 16, each with Verified by and Falsified by. Offline for most; AC-7 and AC-8 interactive, judged on a live drive with no harness built to automate them. The ac-scan was exercised, not asserted: its first run read only 15 because italics nested inside a bold heading broke the parse; fixed, re-run lists all 16 and exits 0.

FIDELITY LIMIT YOU SHOULD SEE: 2024-12-17 through 2024-12-31 have no columns in the source. The app will show no spending for the last fifteen days of December 2024 and 2024's imported annual total is short by whatever was spent then. No import can recover data that was never entered.

CHECKLIST ACCOUNTING: 7 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed.
